scenes.b: Following the path shown by Sage Narada, Sage Vyasa entered a deep meditation.
In that meditation, a great truth revealed itself to him.
Man needs not only knowledge…
but also devotion, to hold that knowledge within the heart.
To carry that truth to the world, Sage Vyasa began composing a great scripture.
It told of the glory of the Lord, the path of devotion,
a divine river of stories revealing dharma and the truths of life.
But this divine wisdom… who should receive it? Who will carry it to the world?
Sage Vyasa had an extraordinary son. His name was Shuka.
A little monkey, too, was learning to walk behind him… almost perfectly.
From his very childhood, worldly things held little interest for him.
Walking amidst nature… his heart always turned toward the truth of the spirit.
Shuka's heart did not need palaces.
It did not need wealth.
It did not need praise.
He wanted only one thing…
To know the truth.
Everything the world desires failed to attract Shuka's heart.
He did not hate the world.
But his heart was never bound by worldly ties.
Shuka… your heart always gazes toward that supreme truth.
Father… when I learned that this world is not eternal,
knowing the eternal truth felt most important to me.
Shuka's detachment was no ordinary thing.
He resolved to dedicate his life to knowing the truth of the Lord.
The monkey walking behind was still learning to walk… but practice must never stop.
Shuka! Shuka!
Shuka… Shuka…
Out of a father's love, Sage Vyasa followed him.
But Shuka's journey was the beginning of a new spiritual chapter.
Time passed.
Shuka Maharshi, with his wisdom and detachment,
rose to become a great sage through self-realization.
That great scripture composed by Sage Vyasa…
would one day become the story that changes the world.
For there was a great king, destined to hear this Bhagavatam.
And… and…
a great sage, too, was preparing to recite this divine story to that king.
Who was that king? What happened in his life? And why did he have only seven days to learn the truth of life?
